title: Hay Que --- Somebody Has To, and Nobody in Particular

lessons.title: hay que — somebody has to, and nobody in particular
lessons.gloss: "one must" — obligation with nobody obliged, and the second of Spanish's two ways to leave a person out

segments.text: Se habla español left the person out. So did every sign you read. Here is the other way Spanish does that — and this one is about obligation.

blocks.title: Grammar Lens: an obligation with nobody in it

segments.text: hay que + a plain infinitive — one must, you have to, it is necessary to.
Hay que hablar español. — You have to speak Spanish. Hay que comer. — One must eat.
Three words you already own, and no new grammar: hay, que, and a verb in its dictionary form.

What it produces is an obligation with nobody obliged. Hay que hablar español does not say who has to — not you, not me, not them. It says the requirement exists, the way a sign says a thing is forbidden without saying who forbids it.
That is the same move as the impersonal se, and now you have both:

utterances: something happens. Spanish: se habla español. leaves out: who does it.
something must happen. Spanish: hay que hablar español. leaves out: who must.

segments.text: Two constructions, one habit: Spanish is comfortable saying that something is the case without saying who is behind it. English needs a vague you or they or a passive to manage the same thing, and always sounds slightly like it is avoiding the question.

segments.instruction: "Hay que hablar español" then "Se habla español" — both with nobody in them
segments.source: [YOU SAY: "Hay que hablar español" then "Se habla español" — both with nobody in them]

segments.prompt: Say you have to speak Spanish, without naming anybody.
What form of the verb follows hay que?

feedback.correct: No conjugation at all — there is nobody to conjugate for.

segments.prompt: Name the other Spanish construction that leaves the person out.

feedback.correct: One says something happens; the other says something must.
feedback.incorrect: The impersonal se — se habla espanol.

segments.text: "One must eat"? (Hay que comer.) Who must? (Nobody named.) And which other construction does the same? (The impersonal se.) Next: all of it in one place.
